questions.question: Describe why independence is considered a fundamental principle for constitutional bodies. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Independence ensures impartiality of constitutional bodies —protects them from political
  • interference—upholds credibility in governance.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the powers of the National Commission for Minorities. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• NCM investigates minority rights issues —advises government on policies —monitors
  • safeguards for minorities.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the background and reasons for the establishment of NITI Aayog. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• NITI Aayog was set up in 2015 —replaced Planning Commission —aimed at cooperative
  • federalism and policy innovation.

questions.question: Assess the effectiveness of constitutional bodies in maintaining checks and balances in the Indian political system. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Constitutional bodies check executive power —ensure accountability —strengthen
  • democratic balance though challenges remain.

questions.question: Examine the limitations of the CAG in the Indian administrative system. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• CAG cannot enforce recommendations —limited to auditing —depends on legislature for
  • action- reducing impact.

questions.question: Explain the constitutional position of the Attorney General of India under Article 76. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Attorney General is chief legal advisor—appointed by President—enjoys right of audience
  • in courts under Article 76.

questions.question: What is the role of RTI in ensuring transperancy in governance ? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• RTI empowers citizens with information —curbs corruption—enhances transparency and
  • accountability in decision-making processes.

questions.question: Discuss the mechanisms to ensure accountabilty and transperancey of Constitutional and Statutory Bodies in India? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Accountability of bodies ensured through parliamentary oversight—transparency promoted
  • by audits, reports and RTI—judicial review strengthens credibility and public trust.

questions.question: Discuss the constitutional foundation and institutional importance of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• NCST established under Article 338A —safeguards rights of Scheduled Tribes —advises
  • government on policies and monitors implementation of constitutional protections.

questions.question: Describe the structure and composition of the National Green Tribunal. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• NGT comprises chairperson, judicial and expert members —specialized tribunal for
  • environmental cases—structured to deliver speedy, scientific, and effective justice.

questions.question: Discuss the evolution and changing role of statutory bodies in India. / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Statutory bodies evolved post-independence—initially advisory, now regulatory and quasi-
  • judicial—changing role reflects governance needs and citizen-centric accountability.
